bindingProtocol.title: Theory-centered research Atlas
bindingProtocol.invariant: Boundary Theory is the organizing root; the laboratory is its public steward, not its conceptual parent.

projection.title: Boundary Theory and the work it organizes
projection.introduction: Begin with the theory, then follow one named branch into its foundations, lineages, methods, programs, applications, or evidence.

branches.label: Formal foundations
branches.description: The central formal object, its composable structures, and operational facets.

branches.label: Research lineages
branches.description: Established formal, scientific, computational, and professional traditions that supply context and constraint.

branches.label: Methods & formalization
branches.description: The disciplines, methods, and research operations that make the theory explicit and usable.

branches.label: Programs & practice
branches.description: Bounded research and professional practices that develop and test the method.

branches.label: Applications & public use
branches.description: Where the work meets institutions, infrastructure, culture, and public consequence.

branches.label: Evidence & stewardship
branches.description: How work earns standing, remains traceable, and is stewarded for public use and repair.

accessibilityConstraints: Every canonical node remains keyboard selectable.
Branch labels do not replace canonical node labels.
The hierarchy remains available through the domain index when the spatial projection is unavailable.
